guardian.title: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo now deadliest in country’s history
guardian.description:
At least 2,325 people have died from the virus, according to official data, with outbreak on track to be biggest in history

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is now the deadliest in the country’s history, with at least 2,325 people dead, according to government data, surpassing the toll from the 2018-20 outbreak.

The DRC’s public health institute said confirmed cases had risen to 4,945, including 101 detected in the previous 24 hours.

guardian.description:
Eighteen children among the people killed after ferry capsized on Lake Kariba

Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe, taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.

The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba, on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it turned over during heavy winds.

euronews.description: Drought conditions have pushed water levels on Germany's Rhine to exceptionally low levels. The situation is putting pressure on inland navigation along one of western Europe's key transport routes. It comes amid a record-breaking wave of extreme weather across the region.

euronews.description: The Norwegian royal palace said the monarch, 89, has been battling haemolytic anaemia, a blood disorder characterised by the premature destruction of red blood cells.

rfi.description: Sophie Adenot is set to become the first French woman to perform a spacewalk, carrying out a mission to repair a communications system on the International Space Station.

rfi.title: Zambia's President Hichilema wins re-election
rfi.description: Zambia's electoral commission has announced that Hakainde Hichilema has been re-elected President after a race that critics said was tightly managed by his government.

rfi.title: French PM Lecornu says aid available 'immediately' to rebuild fire-hit regions
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Monday announced aid worth €12 million to help residents of the southwest hit by wildfires rebuild their lives. He was heckled earlier in the day by dozens of locals in the town of Le Porge in the Gironde region, who said they were unhappy with the government's response.

rfi.title: Iran bars two French diplomats over alleged 'interference'
rfi.description: Iran has said ​that two French embassy employees who were briefly detained last month following a ​diplomatic dispute will not be allowed to return to Iran.

rfi.title: Cop17 aims to restore land and hope in fight against desertification
rfi.description: Extreme weather across much of Europe and elsewhere is lending added weight to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (Cop17), which begins on Monday in Mongolia. RFI looks at what's at stake worldwide.

rfi.title: Migrants stranded in Ceuta say ‘I’d rather die here than go back to Morocco’
rfi.description: Nearly three weeks after a mass border crossing brought tens of thousands of migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, thousands remain stranded in precarious conditions, Maria Jimenez, spokesperson for the NGO Elin, told RFI. She said many still lack adequate shelter, food and medical care.

rfi.title: Devastated by wildfire, the village of Le Porge pins hopes for support on PM visit
rfi.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will visit the Gironde department in southwestern France on Monday to launch reconstruction efforts, after the area fell victim to the most destructive wildfires seen in 70 years. The mayor of Le Porge – one of the villages worst affected – told RFI he's hoping for government support to rebuild its economy, which relies heavily on forest exploitation.

rfi.title: Cameroon beat Malawi to claim maiden Women’s Cup of Nations title
rfi.description: Cameroon claimed a first Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title when they beat Malawi 3-0 in Sunday's final in Morocco, with Marie Ngah Manga’s first-half double helping the the Indomitable Lionesses seal victory.

rfi.title: Ex-PM Attal urges Macron to put under-15 social media ban to referendum
rfi.description: Gabriel Attal has called on President Emmanuel Macron to put a proposed ban on social media for children under 15 directly to French voters, after the Constitutional Council struck down legislation approved by parliament.

rfi.title: Belgium turns to European air support as wildfire rages near German border
rfi.description: Belgium called in aerial reinforcements from across Europe on Sunday as firefighters battled the country’s largest wildfire in more than a century, with flames spreading rapidly through a difficult-to-reach nature reserve near the German border.

rfi.title: Europe's shrinking rivers give rise to debate over how to tackle drought
rfi.description: Europe's shrinking rivers are disrupting industry, reducing power generation and intensifying the debate over how to respond to worsening drought. As water levels fall across the continent, authorities and businesses alike are looking for ways to keep freight moving and critical infrastructure operating. Hydrologists warn, however, that digging rivers deeper cannot create more water and could make shortages worse.

rfi.title: Solar-powered community gardens offer lifeline in drought-hit Zimbabwe
rfi.description: At a shared garden in eastern Zimbabwe, solar-powered pumps are helping farmers grow crops year round, even when drought dries out other fields.

rfi.title: Obesity rises sharply as French Polynesia faces chronic health challenges
rfi.description: French Polynesia is facing growing public health pressures as rising rates of chronic disease combine with an ageing population and changing lifestyles. More than half of adult residents are now considered obese.

rfi.title: Morocco arrests nearly 300 migrants near Ceuta amid renewed crossing fears
rfi.description: Scores of would-be migrants, most of them from sub-Saharan Africa, were intercepted in northern Morocco near the border with the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Saturday, two weeks after tens of thousands of people attempted to enter the territory.

rfi.title: France probes unprecedented cyberattack after tax data of 678,000 users stolen
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a major cyberattack on the country’s tax administration that affected nearly 700,000 individuals and businesses, authorities said on Saturday.

rfi.title: France's successive heatwaves show strain of living in urban 'heat islands'
rfi.description: As France experiences its latest heatwave, residents of urban "heat islands" – dense neighbourhoods with few trees or green spaces – are suffering acutely in the high temperatures, and local authorities are searching for solutions.

rfi.title: Algeria edge Morocco on penalties in WAFCON third-place play-off
rfi.description: Morocco endured a second painful penalty shootout defeat in the space of four days as Algeria claimed third place at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations on Saturday following a 1-1 draw in Rabat.

rfi.title: Armenian Genocide survivors' grandson says 'political motives' block recognition
rfi.description: In 1915, the Ottoman Empire began the systematic deportation and massacre of its Armenian population. As many as 1.5 million Armenians were killed – widely regarded by historians as the twentieth century's first genocide, and the event for which the term was later coined. Stephan Pechdimaldji, the grandson of two of the survivors, spoke to RFI about why recognition still matters.

lemonde.title: La FIFA licencie le Français Kevin Lamour, numéro trois de l’instance, qui s’est opposé à Gianni Infantino

lemonde.title: « Toute la région s’est retrouvée éclairée par les flammes » : les habitants du sud du Liban vivent dans la peur des frappes israéliennes et des incendies qu’elles provoquent
lemonde.description: Dans la zone sous contrôle israélien, les pompiers libanais ont besoin d’une autorisation pour intervenir. Dans les villages encore habités, les résidents se sentent isolés et craignent de devoir quitter leurs logements.

lemonde.title: La scène de la rupture dans « Bérénice » jouée par Marie-Sophie Ferdane : « Tous les mots comptent double ou triple. Tous sont essentiels »
lemonde.description: « Anatomie d’un monologue » (2/7). En 2006, la jeune comédienne se glisse dans la peau de la reine de Palestine, sous la direction de Jean-Louis Martinelli, au Théâtre des Amandiers, à Nanterre.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle : Gérald Darmanin ne sera pas candidat et apporte son soutien à Edouard Philippe

lemonde.title: Mgr Etienne Guillet, évêque de Saint-Denis, un homme « qui crée de la maille là où il y a des déchirures »
lemonde.description: Dans son diocèse de Seine-Saint-Denis, un département où le catholicisme est minoritaire, le plus jeune évêque de France favorise le rapprochement entre les religions. Il prépare la venue du pape au Stade de France, le 25 septembre, dans un esprit d’ouverture.

lemonde.title: La Côte d’Opale fait le plein, profitant de l’été caniculaire dans le reste de la France : « Wimereux va devenir comme Saint-Tropez ! »

Suite des témoignages recueillis par notre envoyée spéciale à  Kaboul.

lemonde.title: Au Texas, Donald Trump suspend un projet de sécurisation de la frontière avec le Mexique dans le parc national Big Bend
lemonde.description: Très critiqué par les habitants et des élus locaux, le plan prévoyait d’installer des barrières, des dispositifs d’éclairage et des technologies de détection au sein de cet espace protégé.

lemonde.title: Paramount réclame une caution de 1,9 milliard de dollars aux douze Etats américains s’opposant à sa fusion avec Warner Bros
lemonde.description: Le rachat par le groupe de David Ellison de son concurrent est contesté en justice par des Etats démocrates, ainsi que par le syndicat des scénaristes. La fusion des deux studios hollywoodiens est suspendue jusqu’au procès, prévu en mars 2027.

lemonde.title: Brésil : Lula salue la découverte de pétrole au large de l’Amazonie, qu’il qualifie de « passeport pour l’avenir »

zeit.description: Menschen in Altersteilzeit nutzen überwiegend das Blockmodell, bei dem die Lohnauszahlung gestreckt wird. Die Rentenkommission sieht eine Abschaffung dieses Modells vor.

Alicja Kwade: »Zieh jeden Abend einen Pyjama an«
zeit.description: Die Künstlerin Alicja Kwade verrät, was sie gerne früher im Leben gewusst hätte. Dass man sich New York zutrauen sollte. Oder wie viel wir mit Zebrafischen gemein haben.

Wetter: Graue Tage in Berlin und Brandenburg
Wahl in Sambia: Amtsinhaber Hakainde Hichilema gewinnt Präsidentschaftswahl in Sambia
zeit.description: Hakainde Hichilema bleibt Präsident von Sambia. Laut Wahlkommission erhielt er etwa 60 Prozent der Stimmen. Die EU hat Unregelmäßigkeiten bei der Wahl kritisiert.

Tennis: Masters in Cincinnati: Zverev zieht ins Achtelfinale ein

zeit.title: USA: Eine Tote durch Tropensturm Lala auf Hawaii
zeit.description: Eine Frau wurde in Zusammenhang mit dem Tropensturm Lala tot aufgefunden. Durch das Unwetter waren 100.000 Haushalte ohne Strom, etwa 100 Häuser wurden weggespült.

zeit.title: Podcast »Alles gesagt?«: Katja Hoyer, wie zerbricht eine Demokratie?
zeit.description: Sie zählt zu den bekanntesten Historikerinnen des Landes. Im Podcast spricht sie über Radikalisierung, Lehren aus Weimar – und ihre Rolle als Beraterin von König Charles.

zeit.title: Ernteausfall: Trockenheit: Ist die komplette Ernte dahin?
zeit.description: Die Bauern befürchten geringe Ernten oder teilweise sogar den Totalausfall. Und: Der Cambridge-Professor Arday wurde nach einer medialen Kampagne tot aufgefunden.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient en direct : Téhéran juge caduc le délai de négociation de 60 jours avec Washington
france24fr.description: Le ministère iranien des Affaires étrangères a déclaré que le délai de 60 jours prévu par le protocole d’accord de juin, pour parvenir à un compromis avec les États-Unis sur le nucléaire et les sanctions imposées à Téhéran, était désormais caduc, en raison des "violations" commises par les États-Unis. Suivez les derniers événements en direct.

france24fr.title: Meurtre de Tupac Shakur : le rappeur a été tué par "vengeance", selon l'accusation
france24fr.description: Les débats ont débuté, lundi, au procès de l'ex-membre de gang accusé d'avoir orchestré le meurtre de Tupac Shakur à Las Vegas. L'accusation estime que Duane "Keffe D" Davis, ex-figure des South Side Compton Crips, a "planifié" l'assassinat par "vengeance" car il nourrissait une "colère viscérale" à l'encontre du rappeur pour avoir humilié son neveu.

france24fr.title: Le président sortant Hakainde Hichilema réélu à la tête de la Zambie avec 60 % des voix
france24fr.description: Le président sortant de Zambie, Hakainde Hichilema, reste au pouvoir. La commission électorale a annoncé, mardi, qu'il a recueilli 60 % des voix lors de l'élection présidentielle organisée la semaine dernière, contre 38 % pour son principal adversaire Brian Mundubile. Le scrutin a suscité des interrogations en raison de l'arrestation d'opposants.

france24fr.title: Au Texas, Donald Trump suspend un projet controversé de barrières à la frontière mexicaine
france24fr.description: Le chef de la police aux frontières américaine a annoncé, lundi, suspendre le projet de sécurisation de la frontière avec le Mexique dans le parc national Big Bend au Texas afin de "procéder à une évaluation personnelle". Le dispositif était très critiqué par des habitants et des élus locaux.

france24fr.title: N.3 de la Fifa, le Français Kevin Lamour quitte son poste après s'être opposé à Gianni Infantino
france24fr.description: La Fédération internationale de football a annoncé, lundi, la fin du contrat de son directeur général des opérations, le Français Kevin Lamour. Il a été l'une des voix les plus haut placées à critiquer le projet de Gianni Infantino d'ouvrir la Fifa à des investisseurs privés – depuis abandonné – et l'auteur d’un communiqué cinglant à ce sujet fin juillet.

france24fr.title: Le Sénégal adopte une loi sur le patrimoine du chef de l'Etat et du président du Parlement
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, la passe d'armes entre le pouvoir exécutif de Bassirou Diomaye Faye et le pouvoir législatif d'Ousmane Sonko s'est poursuivi à l'Assemblée nationale, avec une proposition de loi sur l'obligation d'une déclaration de patrimoine. Celle-ci visait dans un premier temps seulement le chef de l'État, avant que le gouvernement ne l'élargisse aux autres présidents d'institutions. La proposition a été finalement adoptée par une large majorité. Les détails avec Elimane Ndao.

france24fr.title: Gaza : Kushner rencontre Netanyahu pour tenter de sortir le plan Trump de l'impasse
france24fr.description: Jared Kushner, émissaire américain et gendre du Donald Trump, a clôturé lundi deux jours de rencontres avec les dirigeants israéliens et ceux du ​Hamas mais aucun signe d'une avancée imminente n'est apparu, les deux parties campant sur leurs positions. Principale pomme de discorde : le désarmement du mouvement palestinien. Washington et l'État hébreu ont convenu de confier ce processus à un général américain.

france24fr.title: Piratage du Fisc : Lecornu demande un audit à l'ANSSI, 350 000 particuliers contactés
france24fr.description: Sébastien Lecornu a annoncé lundi avoir demandé un audit à l'Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (ANSSI) sur le vol de données ayant affecté la Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP). L'administration fiscale précise avoir commencé à contacter 350 000 particuliers sur les 678 000 usagers concernés par cette attaque revendiquée par le groupe de hackers ZeroBytes.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : l'actuelle épidémie devient la plus meurtrière de l'histoire du pays
france24fr.description: En RDC, l’épidémie d’Ebola a déjà fait plus de 2 300 morts, dépassant le bilan de la crise de 2018-2020, jusque-là la plus meurtrière. Face à l’urgence, les appels se multiplient pour accélérer la mise sur le marché des vaccins encore en expérimentation.

france24fr.title: Cette vidéo partagée par l'agence Reuters ne montre pas un nouvel afflux massif de migrants à Ceuta
france24fr.description: Alors qu'un deuxième afflux de migrants à Ceuta avait été anticipé le week-end dernier, une vidéo censée montrer une foule de personnes se rendant dans l'enclave espagnole dans la nuit du 15 août a été partagée sur les réseaux sociaux et par l'agence Reuters. En réalité, cette vidéo a été filmée le 31 juillet.

france24fr.title: Gaza : Kushner rencontre Netanyahu pour tenter de sortir le plan Trump de l'impasse
france24fr.description: Jared Kushner, émissaire américain et gendre du Donald Trump, a clôturé lundi deux jours de rencontres avec les dirigeants israéliens et ceux du ​Hamas mais aucun signe d'une avancée imminente n'est apparu, les deux parties campant sur leurs positions. Principale pomme de discorde : le désarmement du mouvement palestinien. Washington et l'État hébreu ont convenu de confier ce processus à un général américain.

france24fr.title: À Ceuta, des migrants bloqués aux portes de l'Europe attendent de connaître leur sort
france24fr.description: L'enclave espagnole située en Afrique du Nord a vu, fin juillet, des milliers de migrants arriver sur son territoire. Certains d'entre eux se sont installés sur la plage El Trampolin, à Ceuta. Ces personnes de différentes nationalités, qui parlent des langues diverses, vivent dans des conditions sommaires sur cette bande de sable. L'Europe leur semble très proche, mais leur avenir est incertain et la crainte de l’expulsion est permanente.

france24fr.title: La SAPE à l'honneur à la 6e édition de la DRC Fashion Week à Kinshasa
france24fr.description: La mode congolaise à l’honneur à Kinshasa avec la 6e édition de la DRC Fashion Week. Jeunes créateurs de RDC et du Congo-Brazza y célèbrent notamment la SAPE, mouvement culturel et vestimentaire emblématique, né au début du XXe siècle.

france24fr.title: Russie : vague d'arrestations lors d'un rassemblement de soutien à un parti antiguerre
france24fr.description: Des dizaines de personnes ont été arrêtées lundi à Moscou en marge d'un rassemblement de soutien au seul parti antiguerre de Russie, Iabloko, exclu des prochaines législatives. Dans une procédure distincte, le vice président de cette formation politique, Lev Chlosberg, a été condamné à 11 ans et un mois de prison après des propos critiquant l'invasion russe de l'Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Incendies : Lecornu annonce un plan d'aide qui pourrait dépasser 100 millions d'euros
france24fr.description: Après les mégafeux qui ont ravagé la Gironde et les Landes, Sébastien Lecornu promet de sortir "l’artillerie lourde". Le Premier ministre français a annoncé un plan d’aide qui pourrait dépasser 100 millions d’euros.

france24fr.title: Dans l'est de la France, des plantes pour dépolluer des sites industriels désaffectés
france24fr.description: Depuis 2022, la commune d'Uckange en Moselle, région réputée pour son passé industriel, est devenue un laboratoire à ciel ouvert de la phytoremédiation, une technique naturelle et écologique de dépollution des sols grâce aux plantes et aux micro-organismes.

france24fr.title: Devenu Rassemblement national, le parti de Marine Le Pen élargit son audience (2/3)
france24fr.description: De la dédiabolisation à la présidentialisation du RN (2/3). Une nouvelle étape de l’ascension du parti d’extrême s'ouvre entre 2017 et 2022 avec la volonté de Marine Le Pen de rassurer les Français pour continuer à élargir son électorat. La patronne du Rassemblement national, qui lance durant cette période Jordan Bardella sur le devant de la scène, est par ailleurs bien aidée par un contexte socio-économique compliqué mais favorable à son parti.

france24fr.title: Au Sénégal, une nouvelle hausse des prix du carburant suscite l'inquiétude à Dakar
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Au Sénégal, une nouvelle hausse des prix du carburant suscite des réactions à Dakar. Depuis samedi, l’essence est passé à 990 francs CFA (+70) et le gasoil à 755 francs (+75). Le gouvernement évoque la flambée des cours du pétrole liée au conflit au Moyen-Orient.

KOMMENTAR - Machtkampf um Infantino: Den Herrschern des Fussballs fehlt eine Streitkultur
nzz.description: Die Funktionäre der Uefa und anderer Verbände sollten mit der Fifa konstruktiv über die Zukunft des Fussballs diskutieren, statt ständig vor dessen Kollaps zu warnen. Mantraartig den Rücktritt von Gianni Infantino zu fordern, zeugt von ernüchternder Einfallslosigkeit.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Hitzeschutz ist wichtig, aber er gehört nicht in das Grundgesetz
nzz.description: Die SPD will den Hitzeschutz und die Klimaanpassung in die Verfassung schreiben. Das würde das Grundgesetz mit fragwürdigen politischen Wunschvorstellungen überfrachten.

nzz.title: Frankreichs Verfassungsrat kippt Social-Media-Verbot für Jugendliche
nzz.description: Das von der Macron-Regierung lancierte Gesetz hielt einer Klage der linksradikalen Partei LFI nicht stand. Diese begründete ihren Rekurs mit der Meinungsfreiheit. Im Wahlkampf setzt die Partei stark auf die sozialen Netzwerke.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Trump düpiert Südkorea. Peking hat aber keinen Grund zur Freude
nzz.description: Trump will die Militärübung mit Südkorea substanziell kürzen, aus Rücksicht auf seine «gute Beziehung» mit Kim Jong Un. Für China steigen damit längerfristig die Sicherheitsrisiken.

nzz.title: Kurz vor Saisonbeginn: Leon Goretzka und Ricardo Rodríguez sind noch vereinslos – ein anderer hofft auf ein besseres Angebot
nzz.description: Der Transfermarkt ist eng: Selbst etablierte Fussballprofis tun sich schwer, einen passenden neuen Klub zu finden.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Prozess gegen Pierin Vincenz droht sich in einer juristischen Endlosschleife zu verlieren
nzz.description: Im Berufungsprozess gegen den ehemaligen Raiffeisen-Chef Pierin Vincenz und weitere Mitbeschuldigte schenken sich die Anklage und die Verteidigung nichts. Für das Vertrauen in die Schweizer Justiz ist es wichtig, dass der Fall endlich sauber abgeschlossen werden kann.

nzz.title: Elektrisches Mountainbike von Propain im Test: Dieses Velo erfüllt höchste Ansprüche
nzz.description: Ob günstiges Standardmodell oder frei konfiguriert: Gäbe es einen Preis für das schönste E-MTB – das Propain Sresh SL hätte Chancen. Ob auch sonst alles gut ist, klärt der Fahrbericht.

nzz.title: Zhu Rongjis gemischtes Erbe: Der verstorbene frühere Ministerpräsident trägt die Schuld an einigen der grössten Probleme Chinas
nzz.description: Die Verdienste des ebenso charismatischen wie reformfreudigen Politikers sind unbestritten. Doch Zhu Rongji legte auch die Saat für die Immobilienblase, und die Menschen auf dem Land wurden durch seine Politik ärmer.

nzz.title: Indiens Autofahrer revoltieren gegen den Biotreibstoff E20 – sie fürchten Schäden am Motor und eine geringere Reichweite
nzz.description: Die indische Regierung bewirbt die Einführung des Benzin-Ethanol-Gemischs als Beitrag zum Kampf gegen den Klimawandel und zur wirtschaftlichen Autonomie des Landes. Auf den Strassen sind aber viele nicht überzeugt.

nzz.title: 9/11 prägt Amerika bis heute. Auch deshalb kann Trump den Iran-Krieg nicht gewinnen
nzz.description: Nach den Terroranschlägen vom 11. September 2001 begannen die USA zwei Kriege. Afghanistan und Irak sollten die amerikanische Aussenpolitik nachhaltig verändern. Teil 2 der «NZZ Pro»-Serie zu 9/11.

nzz.title: Vier KI-Modelle machen den Wahl-O-Mat für Sachsen-Anhalt. Bei einer Partei sind sich alle einig
nzz.description: Haben KI-Modelle eine politische Schlagseite? Die NZZ hat vier getestet.

nzz.title: Spurensicherung nach dem Sex: Annie Ernaux zeigt sich immer unverhüllter
nzz.description: Die französische Autorin litt an Brustkrebs, als sie sich in eine Affäre mit dem Fotografen Marc Marie stürzte. Wieder literarisiert Ernaux intimste Erfahrungen, um sich des Lebens zu versichern.

nzz.title: Diese Materie kommt ohne Quarks aus: Forscher entdecken ein Teilchen, das nur aus Kraft besteht
nzz.description: Seit fünfzig Jahren suchen Teilchenphysiker nach sogenannten Glueballs. Jetzt haben sie einen Kandidaten gefunden, der alle wesentlichen Merkmale besitzt. Der Fund bestätigt, wie merkwürdig die Kraft ist, ohne die es uns nicht gäbe.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Politik muss für Gerechtigkeit stehen – Geben und Nehmen sichert den Zusammenhalt
nzz.description: Stabilität und Zusammenhalt moderner Gesellschaften beruhen nicht auf absoluter Gleichheit, sondern auf Konditionalität. Dieses Geben und Nehmen soll ein nachvollziehbares Gleichgewicht bilden.

nzz.title: Plötzlich zwei Milliarden mehr – Konzerne liefern dem Bund deutlich mehr Steuern ab als erwartet
nzz.description: Das Schweizer Geschäftsmodell lebt. Die Steuereinnahmen von Firmen erreichen ein Ausmass, das sich nicht so leicht erklären lässt. Das Finanzdepartement ringt sich dazu durch, optimistischer zu budgetieren.

observador.title: Pavlidis vira Ulisses na Odisseia por Rio Maior
observador.description: Meia dúzia +1, três foram do avançado grego, na goleada (7-0) do Benfica em Rio Maior. Águias somam primeira vitória no campeonato. Ainda, antes de começar a época Barcelona já vence no "El Clásico".

observador.title: Só o Livre, o PCP e o BE queriam o regresso do Estado à REN
observador.description: O DN escreve que só nos programas eleitorais dos três partidos mais à esquerda no hemiciclo é que se encontram referências à recompra da REN. No Brasil, Lula da Silva aplaude descoberta de petróleo.

observador.title: 6h. Sete incêndios a Norte combatidos por 2.000 operacionais
observador.description: Há cinco fogos ativos e outros dois em fase de resolução. É em Torre de Moncorvo (Bragança) onde se concentram mais bombeiros. Ainda, Federação de Ciclismo saúda PGRn por abertura de inquérito.

observador.title: Três reformas que tentaram mudar Portugal
observador.description: Já que muito se fala em reformas estruturais, um ouvinte lançou-nos este desafio: olhar para a História de Portugal e analisar as reformas que maior impacto tiveram no país. Nós escolhemos três delas

observador.title: Qual o plano do governo com a reentrada na REN?
observador.description: Portugal regressa ao capital da REN com a aquisição de 13,7% da energética. Os objetivos do governo podem ser cumpridos com esta participação? Uma conversa com a jornalista Ana Suspiro.

observador.title: 4h. Federação Ciclismo aplaude inquérito sobre Tarling
observador.description: O presidente da Federação Portuguesa de Ciclismo, Cândido Barbosa, fala de uma boa notícia. Ainda, há a esta hora 7 incêndios considerados mais significativos pela proteção civil.

observador.title: 3h. Erdogan pede que Trump continue negociações com o Irão
observador.description: O presidente turco oferece ainda o apoio de Ancara aos esforços de paz. Ainda, o incêndio de Valongo já está em fase de resolução.

observador.title: 2h. Incêndio de Valongo já entrou em fase de resolução
observador.description: Por esta hora o fogo é combatido por 120 operacionais, apoiados por 40 meios terrestres. Ainda, no Médio Oriente vivem-se momentos de tensão entre os aliados árabes dos EUA e Donald Trump,

observador.title: 1h. Benfica vence Casa Pia por 7-0, em Rio Maior
observador.description: As águias venceram em Rio Maior com golos de Prestianni, Rafa, Pavlidis e Duran. Ainda, o Presidente da Câmara de Albufeira garante que nenhum grupo étnico é excluído do acesso à habitação social.

observador.title: "O Benfica não posto à prova pelo Casa Pia."
observador.description: Casa Pia "sem estratégia" goleado por um Benfica "eficaz" que "aproveitou bem" o entrosamento entre Rafa e Pavlidis. Gabriel Alves destaca ainda a excelência de Prestianni no um para um.

observador.title: Casa Pia x Benfica. "Sete golos, todos legais."
observador.description: Nota 6 para João Pinheiro na goleada do Benfica ao Casa Pia. "Arbitragem positiva, mas com falhas": amarelos por mostrar, faltas por assinalar e tempo adicional abaixo do devido.

observador.title: Estamos a censurar o sucesso de Montenegro?
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro mostrou-se desapontado com o retrato que se dá do país e escolheu os grandes números da economia para mostrar que tudo vai bem. Esqueceu-se do resto.

observador.title: Crónica estival ou uma definição política
observador.description: Chegados a meio de Agosto, sentei-me ao computador e achei que, ao fim de cinco anos de crónicas, devia ao leitor uma apresentação e um enquadramento político. Para a semana volto à maçadoria habitual

observador.title: Censura moderna
observador.description: Montenegro queixou-se da comunicação social seguir os princípios básicos do jornalismo em vez do critério editorial do Povo Livre. Ao fazê-lo acabou por alimentar o jogo que diz não compreender.

observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Calimontenegro, o discurso que não tem Pontal por onde pegar
observador.description: Montenegro esteve muito bem ao aproveitar um discurso transmitido integralmente por todos os canais de notícias para se queixar da qualidade da cobertura noticiosa de que é alvo

observador.title: Inúmeros Migrantes, Péssimos Políticos, e a culpa é da bola
observador.description: Perante o maior colapso fronteiriço da Europa recente, cinco partidos de famílias políticas opostas descobriram o mesmo alvo: o Mundial de 2030

observador.title: Humanizar não é deixar de exigir
observador.description: Uma empresa que deixa de exigir para proteger as pessoas acabará, mais cedo ou mais tarde, por deixar de conseguir proteger as pessoas.

spiegel.title: Tennis: Serena und Venus Williams verlieren Doppel-Comeback in Cincinnati
spiegel.description: Sie sind beide Mitte 40 und wollten auf dem Tennisplatz noch einmal gemeinsam Spaß haben. Das gelang Venus und Serena Williams beim Comeback als Duo – trotz ihrer Niederlage. Bei den US Open wollen sie wieder an den Start gehen.

spiegel.title: Erdbeben in Kolumbien: Shakira will beim Wiederaufbau von Schulen helfen
spiegel.description: Popstar Shakira hat nach dem Erdbeben in Kolumbien das Katastrophengebiet besucht. Sie setzt besonders auf Hilfe für Kinder, damit sie wieder zur Schule gehen können.

spiegel.title: Russland: Bürgermeister von Moskau meldet Angriffswelle mit Hunderten Drohnen aus der Ukraine
spiegel.description: Die Ukraine nimmt in ihrem Abwehrkampf erneut die russische Hauptstadt ins Visier. In der Nacht sind russischen Angaben zufolge mehr als 600 Drohnen Richtung Moskau geflogen. Kyjiw meldet seinerseits Tote durch Angriffe aus Russland.

spiegel.title: Sozialpolitik in den USA: Der »New Deal« als Wendepunkt in der Sozialversicherung
spiegel.description: Ihre persönliche Freiheit geht konservativen Amerikanern über alles. Als Präsident Franklin D. Roosevelt mit dem »New Deal« in den Dreißigerjahren erstmals Arbeitslosen- und Sozialversicherung in den USA einführte, galt der als Verräter.

spiegel.title: »Freche Mädchen, freche Bücher«, brave Rollenbilder. War die Reihe nicht total sexistisch?
Account-Teilen bei ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini: Ist das erlaubt und sinnvoll? Was kann passieren?
spiegel.description: Accounts bei ChatGPT und Co. mit Freunden oder Kollegen zu teilen, ist nicht erlaubt. Viele User machen es trotzdem – was das Chatten nerviger machen kann und sogar noch ernstere Risiken mit sich bringt.

spiegel.title: News: Dürre und Gemüsepreise, Schutz vor Drohnen, Deutschlands Top-Rating wackelt
spiegel.description: Die Dürre setzt der Ernte zu. Deutschland will besser bei der Drohnenabwehr werden. Ökonomen warnen vor zu hohen Schulden. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Fitness: Eine KI kann Ihr Training planen. Aber ist das gut genug?
spiegel.description: Freizeitsportler vertrauen immer stärker auf Künstliche Intelligenz. Was die Technik inzwischen kann, wo Trainingsapps an ihre Grenzen stoßen – und wie man einem Chatbot geschickt die richtigen Antworten entlockt.

spiegel.title: Hunde und Fitness: Warum Hundehalter gesünder leben – und was sie beachten müssen
spiegel.description: Ob bei Regen, Hitze oder Sturm: Hundehalter müssen immer raus, damit ihr Tier bei Laune bleibt. Wie das die Gesundheit fördert und welche Rassen zum Außenborder für lange Läufe taugen, erklärt Forscher Ingo Froböse.

spiegel.title: Norwegen: König Harald V. muss wieder im Krankenhaus behandelt werden
spiegel.description: In den vergangenen Wochen wurde Norwegens König aufgrund einer Bluterkrankung mit Kortison behandelt. Nun befindet sich Europas ältester Monarch im Krankenhaus. Harald V. ist zwei Wochen krankgeschrieben.

spiegel.title: Einsatz britischer Drohnen in Russland: Russland reagiert empört
spiegel.description: Die ukrainische Armee hat offenbar erstmals mit britischen Drohnen Ziele tief in Russland attackiert. Moskau schickt wüste Drohungen gen London. Und: Eine mutmaßlich russische Drohne zerschellt in der Republik Moldau. Der Überblick.

phys-org.title: Ancient Egyptian tomb shows how burial trends changed over hundreds of years
phys-org.description: The Theban Necropolis, opposite Luxor, consists of more than 400 tombs. In a new Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology study, researchers in Spain examined part of one of these tombs—chamber three in tomb TT 209—to reconstruct how this burial space was used and reused between its construction during the Twenty-fifth Dynasty (754–656 BCE) and the Ptolemaic period (305–30 BCE), when it was abandoned.

phys-org.title: If your career feels chaotic, try this research-based 'workout routine'
phys-org.description: People's ability to successfully navigate career changes depends on their adaptability and flexibility—skills that can be developed through training transition "muscles," according to Sarah Wittman, assistant professor of management at Costello College of Business and of industrial-organizational psychology (by courtesy) at George Mason University.

phys-org.title: Molecular memory: How a mother's age echoes in her offspring's cells
phys-org.description: In humans and many other animals, a mother's age can affect the physical and behavioral characteristics of the next generation. Scientists call these changes maternal age effects, and while they are widespread across the animal kingdom, researchers still don't fully understand how or why they occur.

phys-org.title: Billions of invasive round goby are in the Great Lakes. Researchers want to stop them from spreading inland
phys-org.description: For decades, the round goby has been one of the Great Lakes' most destructive invasive species. Scientists estimate its population numbers in the billions, making eradication unrealistic.

phys-org.title: Can telecoms turn data into action? Seven-dimension model maps readiness
phys-org.description: Research in the International Journal of Business Information Systems discusses a sector-specific framework to help telecommunications companies assess how effectively they use big data.

phys-org.title: Immune cells have a 'sense of touch,' scientists discover
phys-org.description: Scientists have long believed that tissue-resident memory T cells—which remain in tissues after an infection has cleared and respond rapidly if the threat returns—are shaped primarily by biochemical signals. A McGill University–led study has now uncovered a previously unknown ability of T cells that could change our understanding of how long-term immunity develops.

phys-org.title: Molecular electromagnetic sensor may enable remote-controlled gene therapy
phys-org.description: The deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) of living organisms contains regulatory elements that control when, where and to what extent specific genes are turned on or off. They can be co-opted to create "gene switches" that hold significant potential for understanding gene expression and for therapeutic applications, particularly for the noninvasive treatment or management of genetic disorders.

phys-org.title: Male Neanderthal pelvises resemble those of modern females, challenging decades-old assumptions
phys-org.description: A new study by the Department of Anatomy and Anthropology at Tel Aviv University, published in Scientific Reports, offers an explanation for one of the striking differences between men and women: the evolutionary development of the modern human pelvis.

phys-org.title: Trying to compete with China could slow global climate action, report warns
phys-org.description: China's dominance of key green technologies is helping to subsidize the global transition to a low-carbon economy, but trade tensions could make it harder for other countries to meet their climate targets, according to a new report led by researchers at The University of Manchester.

phys-org.title: Red blood cells inspire next-generation therapeutic nanocarriers
phys-org.description: Red blood cells serve as the foundation for nanocarriers that show promise in a new study as effective and efficient vehicles for gene therapy, tumor targeting and other medical treatments. Scientists at The Ohio State University have showed that the engineered extracellular vesicles could evade immune cells and target cancer cells, two capabilities that could improve the delivery of future therapies. The study is published in Advanced Healthcare Materials.

phys-org.title: Time-gating technique sees through deep tissue, dense fog, and other obstacles
phys-org.description: From helping doctors detect cancer to guiding self-driving cars through traffic, many modern imaging systems rely on near-infrared light, producing a crisp picture when visible light would scatter and yield a blurry picture. But near-infrared systems struggle when light passes through materials like deep tissue or dense fog, succumbing to the same scattering effect in which photons deviate from their path. Existing near-infrared imaging systems also rely on specialized detectors made from expens

phys-org.title: Researcher is trying to save biodiverse landscapes, one unkempt garden at a time
phys-org.description: You've probably seen it before: A native garden starts out lush and intentional, then slowly unravels. A meadow is overtaken by weeds. Native grasses are cut down to sad little stumps. A pollinator garden somehow loses its pollinators by year two. The vision was there. The follow-through wasn't.

phys-org.title: Hubble solves merger mystery from Milky Way's early years
phys-org.description: Our home galaxy, the Milky Way, grew to its current size in part by consuming smaller galaxies. Now, new data from NASA's Hubble Space Telescope show definitive evidence of a dwarf galaxy merging with the young Milky Way in the earliest phases of its evolution. This finding extends our knowledge of our galaxy's history 1.8 billion years farther back in time than before. The results are published in the journal Nature Astronomy.

phys-org.title: A weakening Atlantic Ocean current system could accelerate Earth's warming
phys-org.description: A current system in the Atlantic Ocean that shapes regional climates and distributes ocean nutrients also serves as a control knob to help regulate temperatures across the planet, new research has found.

phys-org.title: Researchers identify ways to reduce the lag between biodiversity data and action
phys-org.description: Biodiversity is enormously diverse, unevenly observed and constantly in motion across space and time. This makes it far harder to monitor than many other parts of the environment. As a result, managing biodiversity often depends on information that is incomplete, delayed or unevenly distributed. At the very moment when rapid change makes timely knowledge more valuable, systems for collecting, identifying, publishing and using biodiversity data often struggle to keep pace.

phys-org.title: Can computers learn what makes the most iconic jazz musicians stand out?
phys-org.description: Machine learning models can identify jazz pianists from recordings and reveal the musical "fingerprints" that make individual performers recognizable, according to a study investigating 20 famous jazz pianists. The research, published in Nature Machine Intelligence, could offer insight into artist attribution and style, cultural heritage, and music education.

phys-org.title: Pesticides make Argentine ants go crazy, sending them roaming or clustering before workers die
phys-org.description: Don't assume an uptick in ant activity after setting out pesticide traps means the treatment failed. New UC Riverside research shows their behavior changes as chemicals make their way through a colony.

phys-org.title: Labrador Sea a key player in providing oxygen for deep North Atlantic life
phys-org.description: Researchers from Cornell University have pinpointed the source of oxygen that sustains deep-sea life in the North Atlantic Ocean: the churning waters in the Labrador Sea.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: Iceland Belongs in the Eurozone
proj-syn.description: In evaluating the trade-offs of joining the European Union and giving up their own currency, Icelanders must recognize that the costs of eurozone membership are smaller than what past data suggest. If anything, being within the eurosystem would make a repeat of Iceland's post-2008 banking crisis exceedingly unlikely.

proj-syn.title: Zhu Rongji’s Legacy of Demographic Decline
proj-syn.description: Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji’s recent death elicited widespread accolades for his role in pushing the market-oriented reforms that unleashed decades of economic growth. But Zhu also oversaw two major policy shifts that have had dire implications for China’s demographic outlook.

proj-syn.title: The Global Land Agenda’s Moment of Truth
proj-syn.description: As delegates gather this week in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, for the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification, momentum is building toward a more ambitious global response to land degradation. In fact, there are five promising signs that this time could be different.

proj-syn.title: How Trump Is Reinvigorating Democracy
proj-syn.description: After a year of commentators lamenting the extent to which Donald Trump had emboldened the world’s autocrats, the political tables may have begun to turn. Not only is Trump deeply unpopular globally, but any government that gets into bed with him is effectively offering proof of its own corruption.

proj-syn.title: Ebola is Back-and the IMF’s Relief Fund Is Empty
proj-syn.description: Once again, the International Monetary Fund finds itself begging for resources to support poor countries facing a public-health emergency. It is an old problem, but one for which there is a remarkably simple solution.

proj-syn.title: What Should Be Done About Asia’s Undervalued Currencies?
proj-syn.description: Those who worry that the renminbi, yen, and won are undervalued vis-à-vis the dollar are usually focused on the large trade and current-account surpluses that China, Japan, and Korea run with the US. But coordinated intervention in currency markets will not address the fundamentals underlying these imbalances.

proj-syn.title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
proj-syn.description: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe than many feared, corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity. To that end, governments should consider what policy incentives are in place, and large employers should consider their own long-term interests.

proj-syn.title: The Making and Remaking of Chinese Totalitarianism
proj-syn.description: For decades, the West assumed that economic growth would turn China into a more open, liberal society, much as it did South Korea and Taiwan. Instead, China’s totalitarian institutions proved remarkably resilient, surviving decades of reform and reasserting themselves under President Xi Jinping.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Not Forget Multilateral Institutions
proj-syn.description: The roadmap for middle-power action that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb recently laid out calls for countries that share interests to create ad hoc coalitions. But to be effective, these coalitions must work as much as possible within existing multilateral institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.
